options.name: comment
options.description: Configures a text string comment to be associated with the instance of this object.  The provided text string will be configured on the object instance.

options.name: extattrs
options.description: Allows for the configuration of Extensible Attributes on the instance of the object.  This argument accepts a set of key / value pairs for configuration. A value may also be supplied as a dictionary to control inheritance of an inheritable Extensible Attribute. Such a dictionary accepts a C(value) key together with an C(inheritance_operation) key set to C(INHERIT) to revert the object to its inherited value, or C(OVERRIDE) to explicitly override an inherited value.

options.name: fqdn
options.description: Specifies the qualified domain name to either add or remove from the NIOS instance based on the configured C(state) value.

options.name: grid_primary
options.description: Configures the grid primary servers for this zone.

options.name: grid_secondaries
options.description: Configures the grid secondary servers for this zone.

options.name: ns_group
options.description: Configures the name server group for this zone. Name server group is mutually exclusive with grid primary and grid secondaries.

options.name: provider
options.description: A dict object containing connection details.

options.name: restart_if_needed
options.description: If set to true, causes the NIOS DNS service to restart and load the new zone configuration.

options.name: state
options.description: Configures the intended state of the instance of the object on the NIOS server.  When this value is set to C(present), the object is configured on the device and when this value is set to C(absent) the value is removed (if necessary) from the device.

options.name: view
options.description: Configures the DNS view name for the configured resource.  The specified DNS zone must already exist on the running NIOS instance prior to configuring zones.

options.name: zone_format
options.description: Create an authorative Reverse-Mapping Zone which is an area of network space for which one or more name servers-primary and secondary-have the responsibility to respond to address-to-name queries. It supports reverse-mapping zones for both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
